newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TENNIS-PIOLINE CLINCHES SECOND TITLE OF CAREER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIOLINE CLINCHES SECOND TITLE OF CAREER.

text.p: France's Cedric Pioline won the second ATP Tour tournament of his career on Sunday, beating hometown favourite Bohdan Ulihrach 6-2 5-7 7-6 in the Czech Open.
Pioline, who lost his first nine finals before taking the Copenhagen Open in 1996, started well, breaking the Czech's first service game on his way to taking the set.
But in the second set the world number 41 twice failed to make breaks count as third seed Ulihrach fought back with two breaks of his own to level the score at 4-4.

The fourth seeded Frenchman failed to clinch victory with three match points at 5-4, allowing Ulihrach, ranked 23rd in the world, to claw his way back into the match with a break in the 11th game before he served out the set.
Ulihrach, runner-up last year and winner in 1995, gained the initiative early in the third set, pinning Pioline to the baseline and dictating the play.

But Pioline weathered the storm, holding on to force a tiebreak. The two traded mini-breaks before a wild forehand by Ulihrach gave Pioline the advantage he needed at 6-4 and this time he did not relinquish it.
"It was a very difficult match and it could have gone either way so I am happy to win. I hope that I can carry this momentum along and eventually back to Paris for the Open there," Pioline said.
